Chukotka east of 180 degrees grey (nobody) from 1991, Belize interior grey from 1996, South African bantustans grey from 1994: all three drawn as holes.
Mongolia matches Cliopatria's outline; the Mongolia/China/Russia snaps are border-cell slop only.

issues.what: Chukotka east of the 180th meridian (about 400 cells) becomes nobody's when the RSFSR ends; Cliopatria's Russian Federation shapes stop at longitude 180.0, so every Russian keyframe snap drops it.
Transkei, Venda and Ciskei (201 cells) released to nobody by the April 1994 vassal_end events and never returned to South Africa.
Belize's interior (75 cells) is still British colonial land in the 1990 anchor and falls to nobody in the 1996 snap; Belize holds only its 10 coastal cells.
The RUF 1993 and 1994 keyframes use a three-cell border band that takes 44 Liberian cells; the page says the SLA pushed the RUF to the border and maps no RUF land in Liberia.
Byelorussian SSR holds 101 cells of Podlachia and Lublin in 1990 (Poland's keyframe loses the size rule); Bialystok was Polish from 1944.

Japan holds seven cells (South Sakhalin, Tyuleniy, Kunashir and Iturup) that Soviet and Russian forces administered; Japan only claims the southern Kurils. The ruling gives them to the USSR in 1990; Russia then inherits them with no later conflict. Japan's claim is not drawn as a contest.
Bophuthatswana vassal_end does not resolve (no gazetteer name); its land is already direct South African land in the draft, so the 1990-1993 vassal tint is missing and nothing is lost from 1994.
issues.decision: left: pages silent on a map region; gazetteer lacks the name

Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan 1991 snaps (Aral Sea, Baykonur lease, border cells) follow Cliopatria's shapes.
Republika Srpska (74 cell-years), Bosnia (19) and Krajina (8) beat Serbia-Montenegro's 1992 keyframe, which reaches into Bosnia and Croatia; the smaller states winning matches the map.
Wa State beats the Union of Burma on 67 Shan cells in 1990; not checked against a page (budget spent on larger holes).

Start anchor p1990: the 75 Belize interior cells are held by british-colonial-empire and the 101 Podlachian and Lublin cells by byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic on 1 January 1990; both come from earlier windows. My events/2 and rulings/0 correct them at the end of 1990, so 1 January 1990 still shows them wrong. If the p1980-p1989 agents fix this the entries become harmless no-ops.

rulings/1 (Japan versus the USSR) settled 7 cell-years; Russia then holds the cells with no later conflict, so no ruling for the Russian Federation was needed. The ruling carries no 'contested' status: Japan's claim to the southern Kurils is not drawn.
